messages:
natalie: FYI CI flagged a microbench regression on PR #12222 — batch_sampler_latency up ~18% vs baseline (> +5% threshold) :grimacing:
ci-bot: perf/bench/batch_sampler_latency: baseline=4.2ms new=4.96ms diff=+0.76ms (+18.1%) threshold=+5% (FAILED) See: https://ci.redwood/bench/12222
samir: omg that's noisy. PR touched kernel-affinity heuristics and the new sampler decay factor, right?
kevin: yes, PR-12222 changed kernel autoselect scoring to prefer affinity when seq_len>1024 and adjusted sampler decay from 0.7 -> 0.55. I suspected this could alter batching distribution.
yuko: can we reproduce locally? I ran the bench a few times and saw variance but not consistent +18%
eng-runtime-oncall: repro steps in the CI job: 
```
# run microbench harness (linux gpu)
bazel run //perf:batch_sampler_bench -- --iterations=100 --model=resnet-lr --seq=128 --warmup=50
# or use perf-runner container
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src ghcr.io/redwood/perf-runner:latest /src/scripts/run_batch_bench.sh
```
samir: I kicked off a bisect on the merge window range (merge-base..HEAD) to find when the delta shows up. preliminary hit at commit abcdef1234 (merge of PR-12195).
ci-bot: bisect job started: https://ci.redwood/bisect/5581
kevin: that commit backported an older kernel selector tweak (affinity weighting). Could be interacting with the new sampler decay in 12222 — cross-effect.
natalie: any flamegraphs or hotpaths from the perf artifacts?
yuko: uploaded top traces here: https://artifacts.redwood/12222/batch_sampler/flame.svg. The flame shows more time in kernel_selector::evaluate_score and in batch_scheduler::walk_queue.
samir: hmm kernel_selector is doing more comparisons per request; looks like affinity path increases comparator work. For small seqs it shouldn't, but batch fanout changed so more attempts to coalesce that cause extra context ops.
kevin: quick patch idea: gate the affinity boost behind batch_size>8 or a latency SLO flag. Could be a safe short-term revert.
natalie: can we try reverting the kernel-affinity back in the bisect branch to confirm? If revert -> perf returns, we know interaction.
eng-runtime-oncall: bisect status: commit abcdef1234 -> fail (regression present). revert abcdef1234 on top of main -> queued for CI.
ci-bot: revert-run: perf/bench/batch_sampler_latency: baseline=4.2ms new=4.25ms diff=+0.05ms (+1.2%) (PASS)
yuko: revert looks promising — regression disappears when affinity change removed.
samir: ok confirm root cause is interaction between PR-12195 (affinity weighting) and PR-12222 (decay). Two options: 1) revert 12195 (short-term), or 2) refine scoring to be O(1) and limit affinity checks per candidate (medium-term).
natalie: ops: rolling a temporary revert on 12195 to unblock. Please open a follow-up to rework kernel_selector complexity and add a microbench that specifically measures selector compare count.
kevin: will open follow-up PR and add test. Also adding a deterministic seed to batch_sampler bench to reduce CI noise.
ci-bot: issue created: INF-1837 "kernel_selector: fix O(N) compare path + selector microbench"
natalie: thanks. Action items: revert rollback -> done, add selector microbench + deterministic seed, plan hotfix to avoid affinity checks on small batch/seq.
yuko: adding notes to the release-blockers doc and will notify releases channel. :white_check_mark:
kevin: one more note: we should also bump the perf CI threshold for this bench to allow for minor noise until deterministic seed lands (proposal: from +5% -> +8% temporarily).
samir: prefer not to relax thresholds; deterministic seed + revert asap.
natalie: agreed. do not relax thresholds yet.
natalie: tagging @eng-platform and @release to coordinate the rollback in the next deploy window.
ci-bot: deploy rollback scheduled for 2026-03-18T04:00:00Z
kevin: thanks — will follow up with PR references and the microbench PR later today.
